A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Memory-V2V work and provide readable text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original novel-view synthesis and long-video editing experiments, quantitative comparisons, and component ablations in Tables 1–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds editing-baseline results and token-responsiveness analyses.

M1.justification: The FOV/DINOv2 retrieval, dynamic tokenizers, adaptive token merging, flow-matching objective, RoPE schemes, and target-video extension pipeline are retained. Expanded explanations and relocated material do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions cover video novel-view synthesis using synthetic multi-camera and public videos, and long-video editing using Señorita-based data. Added comparisons and ablations remain within these tasks. The multi-shot failure scenario already appears in v1.

E2.justification: Table 3 expands long-video editing comparisons beyond LucyEdit variants to TokenFlow, RAVE, and CCEdit, substantially broadening comparator coverage. CUT3R/LVSM variants disappear from Table 2's quantitative comparison, although their qualitative encoder study remains in v2 Appendix C.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 changes the stated 50-video Señorita evaluation split from validation to test; the PDFs do not establish whether samples changed or experiments were rerun. The expanded token experiment adds high-responsiveness controls using top/bottom-50% frame selection and specified overlapping versus unrelated camera trajectories.

E4.justification: The earlier low-responsiveness merging-versus-discarding experiment expands to high- and low-responsiveness interventions, with new plots relating responsiveness to camera overlap (v2 Figures 7–8). Core component ablations remain unchanged. Encoder analysis survives qualitatively, but loses its quantitative comparison rows.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains identical plus/minus entries for responsiveness correlations and overlap. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the new responsiveness plots do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds results for three editing baselines, revealing that RAVE exceeds Memory-V2V on background consistency, 0.9322 versus 0.9233. Table 2 removes CUT3R/LVSM results, including average consistency scores 0.2221/0.2229. Figures 7–8 add responsiveness findings. Numerical values in retained table rows remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The FOV definitions, responsiveness and merging equations, flow-matching derivation, and RoPE/camera-conditioning mathematics are retained. The new empirical analyses introduce no substantive mathematical definition, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The central consistency and editing claims remain. v2 removes the explicit 'first framework' claim, promotes target-only data augmentation to a listed contribution, and explicitly claims scalable conditioning without linear computational growth.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations separating high-responsiveness tokens' role in cross-turn consistency from low-responsiveness tokens' contribution to detail and structure. It adds baseline-specific failure explanations and a limitation concerning large view changes. Multi-shot failures and synthetic-memory artifacts were already discussed in v1.

D1.justification: New Appendix B documents ablation camera sequences, iteration-specific metric evaluation, token-selection fractions, and responsiveness aggregation. Conversely, Section 4.1 replaces explicit task-specific 2K/1K training steps with a less precise joint 1–2K convergence statement, without establishing an actual budget change.

R1.justification: v2 adds CCEdit and RAVE references and removes the MEt3R reference despite retaining that metric. It sharpens the distinction between memory as constraints across independent editing turns and temporal context in autoregressive generation, while retaining the broader related-work coverage.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten. The encoder proof-of-concept moves from the main method section to Appendix C, computational analysis is consolidated in the main text, and new ablation-detail and main-text limitations passages restructure the exposition.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column layout, with widespread resizing and relocation. Encoder examples and computational plots are consolidated, qualitative comparison panels are revised and expanded, table membership changes, and responsiveness plots are added.

improvement.justification: The broader comparisons in Table 3, targeted responsiveness tests in Figures 7–8, and clearer ablation protocols modestly strengthen support for the existing method. These benefits are tempered by removed quantitative encoder evidence, unresolved validation/test wording, and an overbroad superiority statement despite RAVE's higher background-consistency score.
